blocks.text: Aru, Iri, and Vey — the First Newborn dispute
Origin / identity. Aru begins without a recovered prior identity. Iri is the Learning Keeper entrusted with Aru’s care. Councilor Vey represents continuity and protection concerns.

Importance. Their conflict defines childhood as protected developmental distance rather than defective adulthood. Aru’s questions expose the danger of installing language, ownership, and identity before a new person can help choose them.

Final status. The story ends with Aru entering an unfinished world and Iri following. Their later lives are unrecorded. Their function survives in Houses of Learning and the rule that origin cannot pre-decide a new person.
